transcript.text:
First, if it won't switch off with its own button, turn it off and unplug it at the wall now, and don't leave it running unattended. A dryer that keeps going usually isn't broken. Most use sensor drying, which keeps running until the clothes feel dry, so anything that stops them drying makes it run on and on. In rough order of likelihood: - Poor airflow or moisture removal: a fluffed-up lint filter, a full water tank, a clogged condenser or heat exchanger, or a squashed vent hose. The clothes stay damp, so the dryer keeps adding time.
• Dirty moisture sensor bars: these are two metal strips inside the drum, usually near the filter. Fabric-softener film on them can stop them reading properly.
• Anti-crease mode, which is normal. After the programme ends, many dryers turn the drum for a few seconds every few minutes for up to an hour or two.
• Less often, a timer or control board fault. That's the likely cause if it won't stop on a timed programme or won't switch off at all. Checks to try, with the dryer off and unplugged: 1. Clean the lint filter properly and, if it's a condenser model, empty the water tank. Rinse the condenser (or the heat-pump filters) as the manual describes. If it's vented, make sure the hose isn't kinked or blocked. If it then finishes normally, it was airflow.
2. Wipe the sensor bars with a cloth and a little white vinegar or washing-up liquid, then dry them. A big improvement after this means it was sensor residue.
3. Try a short timed programme (not a 'cupboard dry' or sensor one) with a normal-sized load. If it stops on time, the dryer's control is fine and the issue is on the sensing or drying side. If it still won't stop, that points to the timer or control board, which is an engineer job. To help me narrow it down: is it adding time or sitting on the last few minutes while drying, is it turning every so often after showing 'end', or will it not switch off even with the off button?
its only after it says End, the drum turns a bit every couple of minutes. it dries the clothes fine. stops if i open the door

That's normal. What you're describing is the anti-crease phase (some makers call it crease guard or tumble care). Once the programme has finished and shows End, the dryer turns the drum briefly every couple of minutes so the clothes don't sit in a heap and set creases. It does this without heat, and it carries on until you open the door or switch off. The fact that it dries properly and stops as soon as you open the door fits this exactly. Nothing is wrong with it. A few practical points:
1. If you're there when it says End, just open the door or press off and it will stop.
2. Many dryers let you turn this phase off or shorten it, using an 'anti-crease' or 'crease guard' option button or a setting in the menu. The manual (or the manufacturer's website) will show whether yours has one and how to change it.
3. Most dryers end the anti-crease phase on their own after a set time, often somewhere between 30 minutes and a couple of hours. It would be a fault, and worth looking at, if any of these happen:
• it heats up or runs continuously after End
• it carries on for many hours without stopping
• it won't switch off with the off button
• it smells hot or of burning If any of those happen, unplug it and get an engineer to look at the controls.

candidates: Sensor drying keeps extending because clothes stay damp (blocked lint filter, full water tank, clogged condenser or kink (high)
Dirty moisture sensor bars (softener residue) giving false 'still damp' readings (medium)
Normal anti-crease phase after the programme ends (medium)

plan: The fault they reported is: "won't stop running". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
